title: Erdős #101 OQ-01: Four-Point Lines are $o(n^2)$

problemStatement.plain: Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with no five collinear, is the number of lines containing exactly four points $o(n^2)$? Best known: $O(n^2)$ upper (trivial), $\Omega(n^{2-O(1/\sqrt{\log n})})$ lower (Solymosi–Stojaković).
whyMatters: Central open problem in combinatorial geometry.
Connects to Szemerédi–Trotter incidence theorem and sum–product phenomenology.
Disproof of Erdős's conjectured $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ behaviour is itself one of the major surprises of the last 20 years in extremal combinatorics.

proven: At most $(|P|-1)/3$ four-point lines through any single point (fourCollinearThrough_bound, parent file)
open: $o(n^2)$ upper bound — this is the OQ-01 conjecture (1 sorry on `erdos_101_oq_01` in Erdos101OQ01.lean).
Solymosi–Stojaković lower-bound formalisation — 1 sorry on the existential statement (construction over finite fields deferred).
knownResults.goal: Prove $\text{fourPointLineCount}(P) = o(|P|^2)$ for all `NoFiveCollinear P`, or sharpen the bound to an explicit subquadratic rate.

insights: The OQ-01 question is the precise quantitative refinement of the trivial $O(n^2)$ upper bound; the $\Theta(n^2)$ regime is already established elementarily.
Two equivalent formal forms (ε–N primary; rate-witness via $\exists g$) are mutually convertible by the standard Cauchy criterion; we record both.
Solymosi–Stojaković (2013) refuted Erdős's $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ conjecture with $\Omega(n^{2-O(1/\sqrt{\log n})})$ — the open content is the polylog correction, not the leading order.
All known elementary upper bounds are $\Theta(n^2)$; closing the gap to $o(n^2)$ requires either a multiplicity-aware Szemerédi–Trotter refinement or a non-incidence argument.
The ℕ→ℝ cast in `bounds_at_rate_quadratic_over_twelve` weakens $n(n-1)/12$ to $n^2/12$ to avoid `Nat.sub` truncation; asymptotically equivalent.

S6/S7 PREP (researcher-12, 2026-05-15): bridging the slug's strict-< IsLittleOh_n_squared definition to Mathlib's ≤-form Asymptotics.isLittleO_iff is asymmetric. → direction (slug ⇒ Mathlib) is direct via le_of_lt — take Mathlib's universal c as slug's ε. ← direction (Mathlib ⇒ slug) needs (i) instantiate Mathlib's universal c at ε/2 to leave room for strict gap, (ii) max N₀ 1 to ensure (n : ℝ)^2 > 0 (avoids vacuous n=0 case), (iii) mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right. The naive 'ε/2 trick for the → direction' is the wrong assignment — the strict-< form on the LHS of → direction is the *easier* side, not the harder side.
